The tool's declared and fully disclosed purpose is unrestricted process/shell execution on the host: description reads "Run a process on this <platform> machine" and the command_line schema field explicitly documents shell-mode support for pipes/redirects/globbing, while argv gives direct spawn with no shell. run_process.ts spawns command_line via child_process.spawn(cmd, [], {shell:true}) or argv via spawn(argv[0], argv.slice(1), {shell:false}) with cwd/stdin_text/timeout_ms all matching their documented behavior exactly; there is no hidden escalation beyond what the schema/description already promises the caller, so per the anti-false-positive rule this is not itself a finding.
